idiom_name: enum with raw values (+ CaseIterable, failable init(rawValue:))
implementation_notes: Swift enumerations are first-class nominal types, so the language gives the pattern directly: a value of the enum type can never be an arbitrary Int or String, and switch over the enum must be exhaustive. Declaring a raw value type adds RawRepresentable conformance and a failable init?(rawValue:) that returns nil for unknown input, which is the boundary conversion; conforming to CaseIterable provides allCases for iteration. Associated values model payload-carrying cases instead.
pitfalls: The raw-value initializer is failable: force-unwrapping external input reintroduces the runtime crash the pattern removes.
A raw value is part of the wire contract - renaming a case changes its implicit String raw value and breaks persisted data.
For non-frozen enums from other modules, switch needs @unknown default; without it a new case from a dependency is a runtime surprise.
